Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being reminded of the event by others
Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

vignette: Javier, a 26-year-old Latin American man with a history of divorce and current employment as a maid, sought help for his increasing anxiety and distress following an ordeal involving torture. The traumatic event had left deep psychological scars that were now affecting nearly every aspect of his life. The night he was tortured stands out vividly in Javier's mind. He recalls the harsh interrogation, the constant fear, and the feeling of being completely helpless. Since then, certain triggers have become intensely potent for him. Driving past similar cars to those involved during the incident sends a shiver down his spine, and watching related media content on television evokes overwhelming feelings of panic and dread. Even positive emotions can confuse him, as they are overshadowed by the memories of that terrible night. One day, while working at a wealthy family's home, he heard a news report on TV about an incident involving similar circumstances to his own. The story triggered intense flashbacks, leaving him drenched in sweat and hyperventilating. This experience solidified Javier's belief that he needed to avoid reminders of the event by others and stay away from people in authority or uniform. These avoidance behaviors have become a coping mechanism for Javier, but they also exacerbate his sense of threat. He wakes up frequently during the night to check if he is safe and feels an intense alarm when someone touches him unexpectedly. This heightened state of alertness has made it difficult for him to trust others, especially strangers who approach him even in ordinary situations. The cycle of avoidance and threat feeds into itself, creating a self-reinforcing loop. Javier's smoking habit also worsens his anxiety, making it harder for him to manage the stress he feels. As he avoids reminders and authority figures, he finds himself increasingly isolated. He skips social gatherings and has stopped engaging with his former colleagues from work, which has led to further feelings of loneliness and disconnection. One particularly distressing incident occurred when a police car drove past his house one evening. The sight of the vehicle triggered an immediate flashback, leaving Javier paralyzed with fear for hours. This experience solidified his belief that he must avoid any authority figures or uniforms at all costs. Javier's occupational environment has also been impacted by these triggers and maladaptive strategies. During a routine inspection by the property owner, who was wearing a uniform, Javier felt an intense surge of panic and had to leave the premises abruptly. This incident led to strained relationships with his employers and caused significant disruptions in his work life. As time passed, Javier's symptoms escalated, and he found himself increasingly isolated and anxious. His fear of being triggered by everyday events like driving or watching television became overwhelming. He realized that this cycle needed to be broken before it consumed him entirely. What finally brought Javier to seek help was the realization that his quality of life had diminished significantly, and he felt trapped in a never-ending state of vigilance. Javier is most afraid of losing control and reliving those traumatic moments again, but he hopes for relief from these constant anxieties. He seeks support to find healthier ways to cope with his triggers and reduce the pervasive sense of threat that haunts him daily.
